Company.label: Company
Company.description: A business organization represented as a single corporate entity in the supply network. The initial scope is the ten selected publicly traded companies. Supplier and customer are roles a company plays in particular relationships; the same company can play both roles.

Event.label: Event
Event.description: A specific occurrence involving one or more companies at an identifiable time, such as an earnings announcement, guidance revision, or supply disruption. The time of the event is distinct from the publication time of a document reporting it.

Product.label: Product
Product.description: A physical good or named product family that a company designs, manufactures, offers, purchases, or uses, such as a memory chip or a lithography system. Work performed for a customer, such as manufacturing that product, is represented as a Service.

Sector.label: Sector
Sector.description: An economic sector or industry category used to classify a company's business activities, such as semiconductors. A sector describes a field of business rather than a supplier or customer role. The same category may also be used as a Topic when it is a subject of discussion.

Service.label: Service
Service.description: A commercially offered activity or capability, such as wafer fabrication, semiconductor packaging, or testing. This class represents the service offering, distinct from a physical product and from a particular performance or occurrence represented as an Event.

SourceDocument.label: SourceDocument
SourceDocument.description: A specific published document used as evidence for information extracted into the graph, such as a regulatory filing, earnings release, transcript, or news article. A source document is distinct from the companies, relationships, or events it describes.

Topic.label: Topic
Topic.description: A thematic concept used to describe the subject of a source document or the relevance of a company, product, service, or event, such as AI demand or export controls. Topic concepts are distinct from the entities and occurrences they describe. An industry category may also be a Topic. Sharing a topic does not by itself establish a supplier or customer relationship.

buys_from.label: buys_from
buys_from.description: Connects a customer company to a direct supplier company. Inverse of supplies_to.

competes_with.label: competes_with
competes_with.description: Connects two distinct companies that compete in at least one product or service market, as supported by a source document. Competition is mutual but does not propagate through chains of competitors. Companies may also have a supply relationship with each other. Preserve the competitive context in the evidence quote; shared sector or topic membership alone is insufficient evidence.

concerns.label: concerns
concerns.description: Connects an event to a company that is a direct subject of that event. This does not imply that the event affected every connected company or caused a stock-price movement.

has_topic.label: has_topic
has_topic.description: Connects a company, product, service, source document, or event to a relevant thematic concept. Shared topics do not establish supply relationships or measured economic exposure.

includes.label: includes
includes.description: Connects a sector to a company that operates in it. Inverse of operates_in; this property describes sector membership rather than general containment.

mentioned_in.label: mentioned_in
mentioned_in.description: Connects a company, product, service, or sector to a source document that explicitly references it. Inverse of mentions.

mentions.label: mentions
mentions.description: Connects a source document to a company, product, service, or sector it explicitly references. A mention alone does not establish a supply relationship.

offered_by.label: offered_by
offered_by.description: Connects a product to a company that offers it commercially. Inverse of offers.

offers.label: offers
offers.description: Connects a company to a product it offers commercially. This does not imply that the company physically manufactures the product or supplies it to any particular customer.

operates_in.label: operates_in
operates_in.description: Connects a company to a sector in which it conducts business. A company may operate in more than one sector.

provided_by.label: provided_by
provided_by.description: Connects a service to a company that provides it commercially. Inverse of provides.

provides.label: provides
provides.description: Connects a company to a service it provides commercially. This does not identify any particular customer receiving that service.

reported_in.label: reported_in
reported_in.description: Connects an event to a source document describing it. Inverse of reports.

reports.label: reports
reports.description: Connects a source document to an event it describes.

subject_of.label: subject_of
subject_of.description: Connects a company to an event of which it is a direct subject. Inverse of concerns.

supplies_to.label: supplies_to
supplies_to.description: Connects a supplier company to a direct customer company. A chain of suppliers does not establish a direct supply relationship. Product, service, and source details belong on the specific assertion as axiom annotations.

topic_of.label: topic_of
topic_of.description: Connects a thematic concept to a company, product, service, source document, or event to which it is relevant. Inverse of has_topic.

event_type.label: event_type
event_type.description: A category describing the event, such as earnings_miss, guidance_cut, or supply_disruption. These examples are not an exhaustive list.

exchange.label: exchange
exchange.description: The stock exchange for the company's selected listing used in the analysis, corresponding to ticker.

occurred_at.label: occurred_at
occurred_at.description: The date and time the event occurred. For an earnings announcement, use the public release time to align stock returns with the appropriate trading session. Preserve the timezone when known and do not invent a time when only a date is available.

published_at.label: published_at
published_at.description: The publication date and time of the source document, distinct from the time of an event it reports. Preserve the timezone when known and do not invent a time when only a date is available.

ticker.label: ticker
ticker.description: The ticker symbol of the company's selected stock listing used in the analysis, interpreted together with exchange. This is not a globally unique or permanent company identifier.

url.label: url
url.description: A URL locating the source document used as evidence.

evidence_text.label: evidence_text
evidence_text.description: An exact quote from the supporting source document that provides evidence for the annotated relationship assertion. Store the quote as a text literal.

supplied_product.label: supplied_product
supplied_product.description: The IRI of a Product individual explicitly identified by the source as supplied in the annotated supply relationship. Omit this annotation when the source does not identify the product; a supplier's general product offerings are insufficient evidence.

supplied_service.label: supplied_service
supplied_service.description: The IRI of a Service individual explicitly identified by the source as supplied in the annotated supply relationship. Omit this annotation when the source does not identify the service; a supplier's general service offerings are insufficient evidence.

supported_by.label: supported_by
supported_by.description: The IRI of a SourceDocument individual supporting the annotated relationship assertion. Attach this evidence to the specific assertion rather than to the company in general.

ontology.label: Picton interview ontology
ontology.description: A small ontology for describing companies in a semiconductor supply network, their products and services, supporting documents, topics, sectors, and events. The seven core classes are mutually disjoint except that Topic and Sector may overlap. These categories are not asserted to exhaust all possible entities.
